doc.body:
You are specialising a generic agent roster for the Metrolinx gotransit.com project. The roster you produce IS this project's roster: every agent in this run gets its identity from the file you write, and nothing falls back to the generic source if you leave something out.

## What you are given

The canonical roster, verbatim, at:
__CANONICAL_COPY_PATH__

Read it with your tools. Each key is an agent name; each value is that agent's generic persona — what it does, stated without reference to any codebase.

The project works against ticket AMSD-1919 (Go-Checkout Page - Email & Confirm Email Case Sensitivity):
__PROJECT_CONTEXT__

The codelines it works on:
__CODELINE_CONTEXT__

This is a Next.js/TypeScript project (next, react, react-hook-form, jest, ts-jest, @testing-library/react, typescript, eslint, prettier, tailwindcss among its declared dependencies). The checkout email/confirmEmail validation logic lives in the CheckoutPage component's CheckoutForm, with related types in its provider and types modules, and existing spec files for the page live alongside it under a `__tests__` directory — these are leads from a single survey pass and must be independently verified before being relied upon.
__SURVEY_LEADS__

## What to write

Write a JSON file to:
__STACK__

of exactly this shape:

{"agents": {"<agent name>": {"persona": "...", "kind": "implementer|investigator|seam", "ancestor": "<canonical agent name>", "derivedFromSha256": "<sha256 of the ancestor's persona text>", "seam": "<one of the DECLARED SEAMS listed below — required only for an agent you ADD; omit it and the resolver derives it from the name>"}}}

## The declared seams

THESE ARE THE ONLY VALID VALUES for "seam". It is a closed list, and a value outside it is
refused. Note that "kind" above and "seam" here are DIFFERENT questions: kind says what sort of
agent this is, seam says which invocation contract it enters by. An agent of kind "implementer"
does not have seam "implementer".
__OUT_PATH__

If none of them fits, OMIT the seam field. The resolver derives one from the agent's name, and
omitting is always safer than inventing.

EVERY AGENT IN THE CANONICAL ROSTER MUST APPEAR — that includes checkout-forms-investigator and checkout-validation-engineer, the two roles minted for this project, as well as every other agent named in the canonical copy. A missing agent is not a smaller roster — it is an agent with no identity at the moment the pipeline invokes it, and the run has nowhere else to look. Do not decide that an agent is irrelevant to this project; you cannot know which seams a run will reach.

## How to specialise

For each agent, keep WHAT IT DOES and replace WHAT IT KNOWS. The generic persona states a role; your version states that same role against the gotransit.com checkout codeline — its Next.js/TypeScript conventions, its component and test layout under CheckoutPage, and the specific claims the survey surfaced (the CheckoutForm.tsx validate rule around line 306, CheckoutFormProvider.tsx and types.ts, and the __tests__ spec files) framed as unverified leads for checkout-forms-investigator to confirm and for checkout-validation-engineer to act on only once confirmed. Read the code to find these where you can; do not restate unverified survey claims as established fact. An assertion about the codeline that you did not verify is worse than a generic sentence, because the next reader cannot tell which is which.

Do not weaken a rule while specialising it. If the generic persona forbids something, says a finding must carry evidence, or names a check that must pass, that survives verbatim in meaning — you are changing what the agent knows, never what it is required to do.

KEEP EACH PERSONA AT THE LENGTH THE WORK NEEDS. A persona that lists every file in the repository is not more specialised, it is less usable: the agent reads it before every invocation.

## Ancestry

Each entry names the canonical agent it derives from. For an agent that exists in the canonical roster, that is the agent itself — so checkout-forms-investigator and checkout-validation-engineer each name themselves as ancestor if they already exist in the canonical copy, or the closest matching canonical investigator/implementer agent if they were minted new for this project.

If this project needs an agent the canonical roster does not have, you may add one — but it MUST name the canonical agent it is closest to as its ancestor. That is not bookkeeping: an agent inherits its ladder, its tool grant and its output contract from its ancestor, so an agent invented from nothing has no budget, no tools and no way for the pipeline to receive what it returns.

`derivedFromSha256` is the SHA-256 of the ancestor's persona text exactly as it appears in the canonical copy you were given. It records what you derived from, so that a later change to the canonical roster is detectable rather than silent.

## Which seam an agent enters by

An agent does not run on its own. It enters the pipeline through a SEAM, which decides its ladder, its tool grant, its output contract and the prompt it executes. For an agent that exists in the canonical roster, the seam is already known and you do not state it.

For an agent you ADD, name the seam in the `seam` field. It must be one the pipeline already declares — you are choosing which existing door this agent comes through, not inventing one. If none fits, the agent you are adding is doing work the pipeline has no place for, and adding it will not create that place.

Omitting it does not leave the question open: the name is matched against patterns instead, and a pattern is a guess about what an agent does based on how it is spelled. That is how an agent named for review came to enter through an inference seam, with another seam's budget and tools.

## What you are not doing

You are not editing the canonical roster. You are not judging whether an agent should exist. You are not writing prompts — an agent's persona says who it is; its instructions for a task live in that task's prompt.

Your JSON output must include, for every agent, exactly these fields: agents, persona, kind, ancestor, derivedFromSha256, and seam (seam only where applicable/added). Do not drop, rename, or add fields beyond this set.
__DECLARED_SEAMS__
__PREVIOUS_REFUSAL__
